This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version

- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)

# ast-grep(sg) ast-grep(sg) is a CLI tool for code structural search, lint, and rewriting. ## What is ast-grep? ast-grep is an [abstract syntax tree](https://dev.to/balapriya/abstract-syntax-tree-ast-explained-in-plain-english-1h38) based tool to search code by pattern code. Think of it as your old-friend [`grep`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grep), but matching AST nodes instead of text. You can write patterns as if you are writing ordinary code. It will match all code that has the same syntactical structure. You can use `$` sign + upper case letters as a [wildcard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildcard_character), e.g. `$MATCH`, to match any single AST node. Think of it as [regular expression dot](https://regexone.com/lesson/wildcards_dot) `.`, except it is not textual. Try the [online playground](https://ast-grep.github.io/playground.html) for a taste! ## Screenshot ![demo](https://ast-grep.github.io/image/search-replace.png) See more screenshots on the [website](https://ast-grep.github.io/). ## Installation You can install ast-grep from npm, pip, cargo, cargo-binstall, homebrew, scoop, mise, or MacPorts: ```bash npm install --global @ast-grep/cli # `pnpm approve-builds` may be needed pip install ast-grep-cli brew install ast-grep cargo install ast-grep --locked cargo binstall ast-grep # install via scoop scoop install main/ast-grep # install via MacPorts sudo port install ast-grep # try ast-grep in nix-shell nix-shell -p ast-grep # try ast-grep with mise mise use -g ast-grep ``` [Packages](https://repology.org/project/ast-grep/versions) are available on other platforms too. ## Command line usage ast-grep has the following form: ```bash ast-grep --pattern 'var code = $PATTERN' --rewrite 'let code = new $PATTERN' --lang ts ``` ### Examples * Rewrite code using null coalescing operator: ```bash ast-grep -p '$A && $A()' -l ts -r '$A?.()' ``` * Rewrite Zodios code: ```bash ast-grep -p 'new Zodios($URL, $CONF as const,)' -l ts -r 'new Zodios($URL, $CONF)' -i ``` ## Features ast-grep helps you search and replace code based on abstract syntax trees. It can help you do lightweight static analysis and massive scale code manipulation in an intuitive way. Key features: * **Intuitive pattern syntax**: Write patterns that look like ordinary code you would write every day (the pattern is isomorphic to code). * **jQuery-like API**: For AST traversal and manipulation. * **YAML configuration**: Write new linting rules or code modifications using YAML. * **Fast and scalable**: Utilizes multiple cores for performance. * **Beautiful CLI**: User-friendly command line interface. ## Use Cases * **Open-source library authors**: Help your library users adopt breaking changes more easily. * **Tech leads**: Enforce code best practices tailored to your business needs. * **Security researchers**: Write security rules much faster. ## More Information Visit the [official website](https://ast-grep.github.io/) for complete documentation and tutorials. ## Schemas JSON schemas for ast-grep rule configuration are available in the `schemas/` directory. These schemas help you write valid ast-grep rules with IDE support. fn add_ordered(mut cmd: Command, args: Vec<Arg>) -> Command {
    for (i, a) in args.into_iter().enumerate() {
        cmd = cmd.arg(a.display_order(i));
    }
    cmd
}

pub fn run_command(with_config: bool) -> Command {
    let mut args = vec![
        paths_arg(),
        Arg::new("pattern")
            .short('p')
            .long("pattern")
            .value_name("PATTERN")
            .required(true)
            .help("AST pattern to match"),
        Arg::new("selector")
            .long("selector")
            .value_name("KIND")
            .help("AST kind to extract sub-part of pattern to match")
            .long_help("AST kind to extract sub-part of pattern to match.\n\nselector defines the sub-syntax node kind that is the actual matcher of the pattern. See https://ast-grep.github.io/guide/rule-config/atomic-rule.html#pattern-object."),
        Arg::new("rewrite")
            .short('r')
            .long("rewrite")
            .value_name("FIX")
            .help("String to replace the matched AST node"),
        Arg::new("lang")
            .short('l')
            .long("lang")
            .value_name("LANG")
            .value_parser(lang_parser)
            .help("The language of the pattern. Supported languages are:\n[Bash, C, Cpp, CSharp, Css, Dart, Elixir, Go, Haskell, Hcl, Html, Java, JavaScript, Json, Kotlin, Lua, Nix, Php, Python, Ruby, Rust, Scala, Solidity, Swift, Tsx, TypeScript, Yaml]")
            .long_help("The language of the pattern. For full language list, visit https://ast-grep.github.io/reference/languages.html"),
        Arg::new("debug-query")
            .long("debug-query")
            .value_name("format")
            .num_args(0..=1)
            .require_equals(true)
            .default_missing_value("pattern")
            .requires("lang")
            .help("Print query pattern's tree-sitter AST. Requires lang be set explicitly")
            .value_parser([
                PossibleValue::new("pattern").help("Print the query parsed in Pattern format"),
                PossibleValue::new("ast").help("Print the query in tree-sitter AST format, only named nodes are shown"),
                PossibleValue::new("cst").help("Print the query in tree-sitter CST format, both named and unnamed nodes are shown"),
                PossibleValue::new("sexp").help("Print the query in S-expression format"),
            ]),
        Arg::new("strictness")
            .long("strictness")
            .value_name("STRICTNESS")
            .help("The strictness of the pattern")
            .value_parser([
                PossibleValue::new("cst").help("Match exact all node"),
                PossibleValue::new("smart").help("Match all node except source trivial nodes"),
                PossibleValue::new("ast").help("Match only ast nodes"),
                PossibleValue::new("relaxed").help("Match ast node except comments"),
                PossibleValue::new("signature").help("Match ast node except comments, without text"),
                PossibleValue::new("template").help("Similar to smart but match text only, node kinds are ignored"),
            ]),
    ];
    if with_config {
        args.push(config_arg());
    }
    args.extend(input_args());
    args.extend(output_args());
    args.extend(context_args());
    args.push(
        Arg::new("heading")
            .long("heading")
            .value_name("WHEN")
            .default_value("auto")
            .help("Controls whether to print the file name as heading")
            .long_help("Controls whether to print the file name as heading.\n\nIf heading is used, the file name will be printed as heading before all matches of that file. If heading is not used, ast-grep will print the file path before each match as prefix. The default value `auto` is to use heading when printing to a terminal and to disable heading when piping to another program or redirected to files.")
            .value_parser([
                PossibleValue::new("auto").help("Print heading for terminal tty but not for piped output"),
                PossibleValue::new("always").help("Always print heading regardless of output type"),
                PossibleValue::new("never").help("Never print heading regardless of output type"),
            ]),
    );
    let cmd = Command::new("run").about("Run one time search or rewrite in command line. (default command)");
    add_ordered(cmd, args)
}

            .long_help("The language of the pattern. For full language list, visit https://ast-grep.github.io/reference/languages.html"),

            .long("debug-query")

            .num_args(0..=1)

            .default_missing_value("pattern")
            .requires("lang")
            .help("Print query pattern's tree-sitter AST. Requires lang be set explicitly")
            .value_parser([
                PossibleValue::new("pattern").help("Print the query parsed in Pattern format"),
                PossibleValue::new("ast").help("Print the query in tree-sitter AST format, only named nodes are shown"),
                PossibleValue::new("cst").help("Print the query in tree-sitter CST format, both named and unnamed nodes are shown"),
                PossibleValue::new("sexp").help("Print the query in S-expression format"),
            ]),
        Arg::new("strictness")
            .long("strictness")
            .value_name("STRICTNESS")
            .help("The strictness of the pattern")
            .value_parser([
                PossibleValue::new("cst").help("Match exact all node"),
                PossibleValue::new("smart").help("Match all node except source trivial nodes"),
                PossibleValue::new("ast").help("Match only ast nodes"),
                PossibleValue::new("relaxed").help("Match ast node except comments"),
                PossibleValue::new("signature").help("Match ast node except comments, without text"),
                PossibleValue::new("template").help("Similar to smart but match text only, node kinds are ignored"),
            ]),
    ];
    if with_config {
        args.push(config_arg());
    }
    args.extend(input_args());
    args.extend(output_args());
    args.extend(context_args());
    args.push(
        Arg::new("heading")
            .long("heading")
            .value_name("WHEN")
            .default_value("auto")
            .help("Controls whether to print the file name as heading")
            .long_help("Controls whether to print the file name as heading.\n\nIf heading is used, the file name will be printed as heading before all matches of that file. If heading is not used, ast-grep will print the file path before each match as prefix.             .value_parser([

fn severity_arg(name: &'static str, help: &'static str, long: &'static str) -> Arg {

        .value_name("RULE_ID")
        .num_args(0..)
        .require_equals(true)
        .action(ArgAction::Append)
        .value_delimiter(None::<char>)
        .help(help)
        .long_help(long)
}

        Arg::new("report-style")
            .long("report-style")
            .value_name("REPORT_STYLE")
            .default_value("rich")
            .value_parser([
                PossibleValue::new("rich").help("Output a richly formatted diagnostic, with source code previews"),
                PossibleValue::new("medium").help("Output a condensed diagnostic, with a line number, severity, message and notes (if any)"),
                PossibleValue::new("short").help("Output a short diagnostic, with a line number, severity, and message"),

        Arg::new("include-metadata")

        Arg::new("filter")
            .long("filter")
            .value_name("REGEX")
            .conflicts_with("rule")
            .help("Scan the codebase with rules with ids matching REGEX")
            .long_help("Scan the codebase with rules with ids matching REGEX.\n\nThis flags conflicts with --rule. It is useful to scan with a subset of rules from a large set of rule definitions within a project."),
        config_arg(),
        severity_arg("error", "Set rule severity to error", "Set rule severity to error\n\nThis flag sets the specified RULE_ID's severity to error. You can specify multiple rules by using the flag multiple times, e.g., `--error=RULE_1 --error=RULE_2`. If no RULE_ID is provided, all rules will be set to error, e.g., `--error`. Note, this flag must use `=` to specify its value."),
        severity_arg("warning", "Set rule severity to warning", "Set rule severity to warning\n\nThis flag sets the specified RULE_ID's severity to warning. You can specify multiple rules by using the flag multiple times. If no RULE_ID is provided, all rules will be set to warning. Note, this flag must use `=` to specify its value."),
        severity_arg("info", "Set rule severity to info", "Set rule severity to info\n\nThis flag sets the specified RULE_ID's severity to info. You can specify multiple rules by using the flag multiple times. If no RULE_ID is provided, all rules will be set to info. Note, this flag must use `=` to specify its value."),
        severity_arg("hint", "Set rule severity to hint", "Set rule severity to hint\n\nThis flag sets the specified RULE_ID's severity to hint. You can specify multiple rules by using the flag multiple times. If no RULE_ID is provided, all rules will be set to hint. Note, this flag must use `=` to specify its value."),
        severity_arg("off", "Turn off rule", "Turn off rule\n\nThis flag turns off the specified RULE_ID. You can disable multiple rules by using the flag multiple times. If no RULE_ID is provided, all rules will be turned off. Note, this flag must use `=` to specify its value."),

    args.extend(context_args());

pub fn test_command() -> Command {
    let args = vec![
        Arg::new("test-dir")
            .short('t')
            .long("test-dir")
            .value_name("TEST_DIR")
            .help("the directories to search test YAML files"),
        Arg::new("snapshot-dir")
            .long("snapshot-dir")
            .value_name("SNAPSHOT_DIR")
            .help("Specify the directory name storing snapshots. Default to __snapshots__"),
        Arg::new("skip-snapshot-tests")
            .long("skip-snapshot-tests")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .conflicts_with("update-all")
            .help("Only check if the test code is valid, without checking rule output. Turn it on when you want to ignore the output of rules. Conflicts with --update-all"),
        Arg::new("update-all")
            .short('U')
            .long("update-all")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help("Update the content of all snapshots that have changed in test. Conflicts with --skip-snapshot-tests"),
        Arg::new("interactive")
            .short('i')
            .long("interactive")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help("Start an interactive review to update snapshots selectively"),
        Arg::new("filter")

            .long("filter")
            .value_name("REGEX")
            .help("Only run rule test cases that matches REGEX"),

fn new_common() -> Vec<Arg> {
    vec![
        Arg::new("name").value_name("NAME").help("The id of the item to create"),
        Arg::new("lang")
            .short('l')
            .long("lang")
            .value_name("LANG")
            .value_parser(lang_parser)
            .help("The language of the item to create")
            .long_help("The language of the item to create.\n\nThis option is only available when creating rule and util."),
        Arg::new("yes")
            .short('y')
            .long("yes")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help("Accept all default options without interactive input during creation")
            .long_help("Accept all default options without interactive input during creation.\n\nYou need to provide all required arguments via command line if this flag is true. Please see the command description for the what arguments are required."),
        config_arg(),
    ]
}

pub fn new_command() -> Command {
    let sub = |name: &'static str, about: &'static str, long: &'static str| {
        add_ordered(Command::new(name).about(about).long_about(long), new_common())
    };
    let cmd = Command::new("new")
        .about("Create new ast-grep project or items like rules/tests")
        .subcommand(sub("project", "Create an new project by scaffolding", "Create an new project by scaffolding.\n\nBy default, this command will create a root config file `sgconfig.yml`, a rule folder `rules`, a test case folder `rule-tests` and a utility rule folder `utils`. You can customize the folder names during the creation."))
        .subcommand(sub("rule", "Create a new rule", "Create a new rule.\n\nThis command will create a new rule in one of the `rule_dirs`. You need to provide `name` and `language` either by interactive input or via command line arguments. ast-grep will ask you which `rule_dir` to use if multiple ones are configured in the `sgconfig.yml`. If `-y, --yes` flag is true, ast-grep will choose the first `rule_dir` to create the new rule."))
        .subcommand(sub("test", "Create a new test case", "Create a new test case.\n\nThis command will create a new test in one of the `test_dirs`. You need to provide `name` either by interactive input or via command line arguments. ast-grep will ask you which `test_dir` to use if multiple ones are configured in the `sgconfig.yml`. If `-y, --yes` flag is true, ast-grep will choose the first `test_dir` to create the new test."))
        .subcommand(sub("util", "Create a new global utility rule", "Create a new global utility rule.\n\nThis command will create a new global utility rule in one of the `utils` folders. You need to provide `name` and `language` either by interactive input or via command line arguments. ast-grep will ask you which `util_dir` to use if multiple ones are configured in the `sgconfig.yml`. If `-y, --yes` flag is true, ast-grep will choose the first `util_dir` to create the new item."));
    add_ordered(cmd, new_common())
}

pub fn main_command() -> Command {
    Command::new("ast-grep")
        .version("0.42.1")
        .about("Search and Rewrite code at large scale using precise AST pattern")
        .long_about(MAIN_LONG_ABOUT)
        .arg_required_else_help(true)
        .subcommand_required(true)
        .arg(config_arg())
        .subcommand(run_command(true))
        .subcommand(scan_command())
        .subcommand(test_command())
        .subcommand(new_command())
        .subcommand(Command::new("lsp").about("Start language server").arg(config_arg()))
        .subcommand(
            Command::new("completions")
                .about("Generate shell completion script")
                .arg(
                    Arg::new("shell")
                        .value_name("SHELL")
                        .help("Output the completion file for given shell. If not provided, shell flavor will be inferred from environment")
                        .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(clap_complete::Shell)),
                )
                .arg(config_arg()),
        )
}

pub fn default_run_command() -> Command {
    run_command(false)
        .name("ast-grep")
        .about(None::<&str>)
}
